items.title_en: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
items.title_zh: Ropedia W0：以人类经验跨具身扩展移动-操作世界模型
items.abstract_en: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, $Ψ_0$, $ω$-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.
items.abstract_zh: 世界模型可让具身智能体预测动作后果，但跨异构具身联合建模移动与操作，仍受动作空间差异与多模态监督不足的制约。本文提出 Ropedia W0，首个覆盖人类与多种具身机器人的第一人称移动-操作世界基座模型。Xp-Data 含 1 万小时人类第一人称数据与 3000 小时机器人数据，具备统一多模态标注与质量控制；以相机位姿编码移动、投影骨架编码操作，机器人骨架结合正运动学与人工关键点校正。并提出长程基准 Xp-Teleop。在五个跨具身基准与留出人类视频上领先，支持零样本到全量后训练以及实时 VR 交互。
items.highlight_zh: 首个跨人类与多具身机器人的移动-操作世界基座模型
items.digest_zh:
• 问题：机器人在真实环境中既要走动又要用手操作（loco-manipulation）。若有一个能“预演后果”的世界模型，就能帮助规划与决策。但人类、人形、四足、机械臂的动作空间完全不同，带多模态标注的数据又稀少，因此很难训练一个跨具身的通用世界模型。
• 方法：作者提出 Ropedia W0，用统一表示把不同具身装进同一个模型：移动用相机位姿表示，操作用投影骨架表示，机器人骨架则由各具身的前向运动学加上大量人工关键点标注与校正得到。数据侧构建 Xp-Data，含 1 万小时人类第一人称视频加 3000 小时机器人数据，配有统一多模态标注与质量控制。
• 结果：在 DreamDojo、Ψ0、ω-HOME、Xp-Teleop、AgiBot 五个跨具身基准以及留出的人类第一人称视频上，从零样本推理到少样本、全量后训练都取得最优表现；扩大人类预训练数据能同时提升人类与机器人评测成绩；蒸馏后可实现实时、分钟级的推演，支持实时 VR 交互。
• 意义：这说明海量而廉价的人类第一人称视频可作为机器人的“经验”来源；一个模型统一处理移动与操作，可直接用于策略评估、基于模型的规划以及世界-动作建模。

rm.usage: 面向跨具身移动-操作的世界模型与大规模第一人称数据，思路可借鉴到工程机器人视觉装配的模仿学习数据采集与动作后果预测，但模型体量与算力需求远超车载端，短期难以落地到 RoboMaster。

items.title_en: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
items.title_zh: 通过点轨迹预测学习 4D 世界
items.abstract_en: Reliable multi-view forecasting requires videos from different cameras to describe the same evolving 3D scene. To this end, we introduce Video-Point Model (VPM), a world model that conditions on multi-view video histories and a language instruction to jointly forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and the 3D trajectories of persistent scene points. We extend a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing that integrates complementary observations across cameras, and add a trajectory head that predicts how physical points move through time. Each trajectory tracks a single point across all views, and supervising these trajectories alongside video generation therefore anchors appearance changes in every camera to a shared description of 3D motion. To support training and evaluation, we build VPM-Data, a simulation corpus pairing synchronized multi-view videos with persistent point trajectories, and VP-WorldBench, a forecasting benchmark spanning simulated and real environments. We further extend VPM to robot control by adding robot actions as a token modality in the generator. Action tokens share the point-supervised backbone and are denoised jointly with future videos, thereby grounding the policy in the same 3D-aware representation. On VP-WorldBench and existing 4D generation benchmarks, point supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D motion accuracy over a video-only counterpart, and in simulated and real-robot experiments, it also raises the manipulation success of the action-enabled model.
items.abstract_zh: 可靠的多视角预测要求不同相机的视频描述同一演化中的三维场景。为此本文提出 Video-Point Model（VPM）：以多视角视频历史与语言指令为条件，联合预测任意视角的未来视频以及场景持久点的三维轨迹。作者为预训练世界模型加入相机条件的多视角处理与轨迹预测头，每条轨迹跨所有视角跟踪同一点，从而把各相机的外观变化锚定到统一的 3D 运动描述。为支持训练与评测，构建 VPM-Data 仿真语料与 VP-WorldBench 基准，并把动作作为 token 模态接入生成器以扩展到机器人控制。在基准上点监督同时提升视频保真度与 3D 运动精度，并提高仿真与真机操作成功率。
items.highlight_zh: 用跨视角共享的点轨迹监督，让视频预测与 3D 运动一致
items.digest_zh:
• 问题：多视角视频预测的难点在于，不同相机拍到的画面必须描述同一个正在演化的三维场景。只做像素级视频预测的模型，可能每一路画面都很逼真，却在三维上彼此矛盾。
• 方法：作者提出 Video-Point Model（VPM）。它以多视角视频历史和一句语言指令为输入，同时输出（1）任意视角的未来视频、（2）场景中一批“持久点”的三维运动轨迹。关键设计是每条轨迹跨所有视角追踪同一个物理点，于是各相机的外观变化被锚定到同一份三维运动描述上。他们在一个预训练世界模型上加入相机条件的多视角处理和轨迹预测头，并构建了配套仿真数据 VPM-Data 与评测基准 VP-WorldBench。作者还把机器人动作作为 token 模态加入生成器，与未来视频一起去噪，使策略也建立在同一套 3D 感知表示上。
• 结果：在 VP-WorldBench 和现有 4D 生成基准上，相比只用视频监督的版本，点监督同时提升了视频保真度和 3D 运动精度；在仿真和真机实验中，带动作的模型操作成功率也更高。
• 意义：点轨迹提供了一种廉价而明确的 3D 监督信号，把“看起来对”升级为“三维上对”，并让视频世界模型能兼作机器人策略的骨干。

rm.usage: 多视角视频+三维点轨迹的联合预测思路，可用于雷达/哨兵场景下多相机对同一运动目标的 3D 轨迹外推，或作为仿真中预测敌方未来位置的生成式模型，但需大量改造且实时性存疑。
rm.task: 雷达目标探测与信息融合

items.title_en: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
items.title_zh: PVBench：用物体级物理测量量化视频生成的物理合理性
items.abstract_en: Recent video generation models produce visually compelling outputs, yet their physical plausibility remains poorly measured. Physical plausibility asks whether generated objects obey geometry, kinematics, dynamics, and conservation laws. Existing benchmarks rely on coarse visual-language model judgments or target embodied world models rather than video generation itself. We introduce PVBench, a physical video benchmark that quantitatively measures the plausibility of generated videos across 46 dimensions organized into seven domains, spanning: i) instruction and semantic fidelity, ii) behavioral and causal consistency, iii) perceptual and temporal quality, iv) geometric and spatial consistency, v) material properties and field states, vi) kinematic and spatiotemporal persistence, vii) and mechanical plausibility with conservation laws. PVBench comprises 600 carefully crafted prompts, of which 30% involve physical embodied agents such as robot arms, humanoids, quadrupeds, and multi-agent systems. For challenging physically tractable dimensions, it pairs each with specialized vision models that derive verifiable, physically grounded measurements, such as object-level 6D pose, metric scale, surface normals, kinematics, and numerical conservation-law residuals. It thus avoids relying solely on subjective scoring, while supporting both text-to-video and image-to-video generation. Finally, we validate the agreement between automatic metrics and human judgments through human evaluation. Meanwhile, we evaluate mainstream open-source and closed-source models and present several insights. By releasing the benchmark, prompts, and calibration protocol, we aim to foster physically grounded video generation.
items.abstract_zh: 视频生成模型画面愈发逼真，但物理合理性缺乏度量——生成物体是否遵守几何、运动学、动力学与守恒律。现有基准多依赖视觉语言模型的粗粒度判断，或面向具身世界模型而非视频生成本身。本文提出 PVBench，分七大领域、46 个维度定量衡量生成视频的物理可信度，涵盖语义保真、因果一致、感知与时间质量、几何空间一致、材质与场状态、运动学持续性以及力学与守恒律。其 600 条提示词中 30% 涉及机械臂、人形、四足与多智能体等具身智能体；对可量化的维度配套专用视觉模型给出可验证测量，如物体级 6D 位姿、度量尺度、表面法线与守恒律残差，并支持文生与图生视频。
items.highlight_zh: 以 46 维物理量替代主观打分，量化视频生成的物理合理性
items.digest_zh:
• 问题：视频生成模型如今能产出非常好看的画面，但“好看”不等于“物理上说得通”。物体的形状、运动、碰撞、光影、材料是否遵守几何、运动学、动力学与守恒律，此前缺少系统的量化标准。
• 方法：作者提出 PVBench，把物理合理性拆成 7 大领域、46 个维度：指令与语义保真、行为与因果一致性、感知与时间质量、几何与空间一致性、材质属性与场状态、运动学与时空持续性、力学合理性与守恒律。数据集含 600 条精心编写的提示词，其中 30% 涉及机械臂、人形、四足、多智能体等具身智能体。对可量化的维度，他们用专门的视觉模型直接测出物理量——物体级 6D 位姿、度量尺度、表面法线、运动学、守恒律数值残差——而不是只让大模型打分。
• 结果：基准同时支持文生视频与图生视频；作者用人工评测检验了自动指标与人类判断的一致性，并评测了主流开源与闭源模型，总结出若干规律。
• 意义：它把物理可信度从主观印象变成可复现的测量，为“物理一致”的视频生成提供明确的优化与比较方向，也公开了提示词与校准流程供社区使用。

rm.usage: 给出物体级 6D 位姿、尺度、守恒律残差等可量化指标，可借来评估自瞄/装配仿真视频或仿真器物理可信度，属评测方法论参考，与赛场算法本身关联较弱。

items.title_en: Media Intelligence Platform: Multimodal Detection of Synthetic and Manipulated Content
items.title_zh: 媒体智能平台：合成与篡改内容的多模态检测
items.abstract_en: The rapid progress of generative artificial intelligence has led to a significant increase in manipulated multimedia content, including synthetic faces, forged videos, AI-generated images, fake audio, and locally edited images. Existing detection approaches are typically designed for a single manipulation type, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios involving heterogeneous media sources. In this work, we present the Media Intelligence Platform (MIP), a unified web-based framework for multimodal media forensics integrating specialized modules for fake video detection, face morphing detection, AI-generated image detection, audio deepfake detection, localized image manipulation detection, and text analysis. Its modular architecture enables flexible integration of heterogeneous models and supports future extensions for emerging manipulation techniques. Experimental results on representative benchmark datasets demonstrate reliable detection performance across multiple media modalities while providing a practical and user-friendly interface for forensic investigations. The platform highlights the potential of unified multimodal systems for comprehensive deepfake detection in real-world environments, and is accompanied by a public demonstrator released with this workshop submission to support reproducibility and community evaluation.
items.abstract_zh: 生成式 AI 的快速进展，使合成人脸、伪造视频、AI 生成图像、假音频与局部编辑图像等被篡改的多媒体内容显著增多。现有检测方法通常只针对单一篡改类型，难以应对真实场景中异构媒体来源并存的情况。本文提出媒体智能平台（MIP），一个基于网页的统一多模态媒体取证框架，集成假视频检测、人脸形变检测、AI 生成图像检测、音频深度伪造检测、局部图像篡改检测与文本分析等专用模块；其模块化架构便于接入异构模型并扩展至新的篡改手法。在代表性基准数据集上各模态检测性能可靠，平台提供友好的取证界面，并发布公开演示系统以支持复现与社区评测。
items.highlight_zh: 一个网页平台统一检测视频、图像、音频与文本等多类伪造内容
items.digest_zh:
• 问题：生成式 AI 让换脸、伪造视频、AI 生图、语音克隆、局部修图变得越来越容易，但绝大多数检测工具只针对一种篡改类型。真实的取证场景里，嫌疑材料往往混杂多种来源，单一模型难以应付。
• 方法：作者构建了媒体智能平台 MIP——一个基于网页的统一多模态取证框架，把假视频检测、人脸形变（morphing）检测、AI 生成图像检测、音频深度伪造检测、局部图像篡改检测和文本分析等专用模块集成到一起。模块化架构让不同的异构模型可以灵活接入，也便于日后加入针对新型篡改手法的模块。
• 结果：在多个代表性基准数据集上，各模态都表现出可靠的检测性能；平台提供面向调查人员的实用、易用界面。作者还随论文发布了公开演示系统，以便复现与社区评测。
• 意义：它把分散的深度伪造检测工具整合成一个可操作的取证入口，展示了统一多模态系统在真实环境下做综合鉴伪的可行性，同时也回应了“多类型混杂”这一现实需求。
items.comment: ECCV 2026, Workshop on AI for Multimedia Forensics & Disinformation Detection (AI4MFDD2026)

rm.usage: 多模态伪造检测平台与赛场算法几乎无关，至多是赛事反作弊（如提交视频真实性核查）的方法参考，实用价值很低。

items.title_en: PnP-Transformer: A Neural Pose Solver for Zero-Shot 6D Object Pose Estimation
items.title_zh: PnP-Transformer：用于零样本 6D 物体位姿估计的神经位姿求解器
items.abstract_en: We present PnP-Transformer, a neural pose solver designed as an iterative-free, differentiable alternative to classical PnP-RANSAC algorithms. PnP-Transformer regresses the 6D object pose by processing predicted semi-dense 2D-3D correspondence fields alongside confidence scores, while mapping geometric inputs into a continuous latent space. To evaluate its practical utility, we integrate PnP-Transformer into a zero-shot 6D pose estimation pipeline, where the correspondence module and pose solver are trained separately. PnP-Transformer achieves a 41.2% mean AR score with low latency (0.46 s/obj) on seven core BOP benchmark datasets, surpassing all prior baselines (such as RayPose with 39.1% AR) but one (Co-op with 58.4% AR). When the pose solver is replaced with EPnP-RANSAC (similar to Co-op) while keeping the correspondence module unchanged, the RANSAC alternative outperforms PnP-Transformer on six of the seven datasets by reaching 52.2% mean AR at a cost of an additional 60 ms per object, revealing an accuracy-latency trade-off. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/ebylmz/pnp-transformer.
items.abstract_zh: 我们提出 PnP-Transformer，一种神经位姿求解器，作为经典 PnP-RANSAC 算法的无迭代、可微替代方案。它通过处理预测得到的半稠密 2D-3D 对应场及其置信度分数来回归 6D 物体位姿，并将几何输入映射到连续隐空间。为考察实用价值，我们将其集成进一个零样本 6D 位姿估计流程，其中对应模块与位姿求解器分开训练。在七个核心 BOP 基准数据集上，PnP-Transformer 取得 41.2% 的平均 AR 分数，延迟仅 0.46 秒/物体，优于除 Co-op（58.4% AR）以外的所有已有基线（如 RayPose 的 39.1% AR）。若在保持对应模块不变的前提下把求解器换成 EPnP-RANSAC，RANSAC 方案在七个数据集中的六个上反超 PnP-Transformer，平均 AR 达 52.2%，代价是每个物体多花 60 毫秒，体现出精度与延迟之间的权衡。代码与预训练模型已公开。
items.highlight_zh: 免迭代、可微的神经位姿求解器，揭示精度与延迟的权衡
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：在 6D 物体位姿估计中，从图像找到物体上若干点与三维模型点的对应关系后，需要由这些 2D-3D 对应解出物体的旋转和平移，这一步传统上交给 PnP-RANSAC 这类几何算法。而 PnP-RANSAC 依赖迭代与随机采样，不可微分，也无法与神经网络端到端训练。

方法：作者训练了一个 Transformer 式的神经网络来直接“一步算出”位姿。输入是预测出的半稠密 2D-3D 对应点及其置信度分数，网络把几何量映射到连续隐空间后回归 6D 位姿，整个过程不需要迭代，也不需要 RANSAC 的随机采样。他们把该求解器接入零样本位姿估计流程：对应模块和求解器各自单独训练，不在同一流程中联合训练。

结果：在 BOP 的七个标准数据集上，该方法平均 AR 为 41.2%，单物体耗时 0.46 秒，超过了此前多数基线（如 RayPose 的 39.1%），但不及 Co-op 的 58.4%。关键的对照实验是：保留同一个对应模块，只把求解器换成 EPnP-RANSAC，结果在七个数据集中的六个上更好，平均 AR 达 52.2%，只是每个物体多 60 毫秒。

意义：这说明神经网络求解器的优势主要在速度与可微性，便于端到端优化，但在当前设定下精度尚不如经典几何方法；论文因此把一个此前较少被量化的问题摆上台面——位姿求解环节究竟该用学习方法还是几何方法，取决于你对精度和延迟的取舍。对做机器人抓取、AR 等实时系统的研究者而言，这是很实际的工程参考。

rm.usage: 其神经位姿求解器可替换工程机器人装配中科技核心、能量单元、视觉标签的 PnP-RANSAC 位姿求解环节，实现端到端可微的 6D 位姿回归；但论文自述精度不及 EPnP-RANSAC 且单目标 0.46s，只适合静态装配场景，自瞄等高频环节不适用。

items.title_en: HATCH: Hardware-Attested Task Chains for Verifiable Manipulation
items.title_zh: HATCH：面向可验证操作任务的硬件认证任务链
items.abstract_en: Capability claims in robot manipulation are unverifiable, and existing leaderboards are each closed, simulated, or gameable. We propose HATCH, a robot escape room: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable benchmark. Tasks span five skill categories at three difficulty levels and are chained so that the sensor confirming one task's completion unlocks the next, turning a room into a single long-horizon evaluation. Success is confirmed by instrumentation rather than human judgment, scoring is embodiment-agnostic, and object placements are randomized by a run-day seed. Entrants submit attested self-runs (uncut video, sensor logs, and the seed), with occasional organized events for calibration. Task specifications, build guide, bill of materials, and scoring rubrics are released under an open license.
items.abstract_zh: 机器人操作领域的能力宣称往往难以验证，而现有排行榜要么封闭、要么基于仿真、要么容易被钻空子。我们提出 HATCH——一个机器人“密室逃脱”：公开规范、可物理复现、由传感器评分且无法预先排练的基准。任务覆盖五个技能类别、三个难度等级，并被串联起来：当一个任务完成的传感器信号被确认后，才会解锁下一个任务，从而把一个房间变成一次长程评测。成功由仪器判定而非人工判断，评分与机器人形态无关，物体摆放由运行当日的随机种子决定。参赛者提交经认证的自主运行记录（未剪辑视频、传感器日志和随机种子），并辅以不定期组织的活动进行校准。任务规范、搭建指南、物料清单与评分细则均以开放许可发布。
items.highlight_zh: 开放式“机器人密室逃脱”基准：传感器判定、任务链串联、不可排练
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：机器人操作论文常宣称“我的机器人会做某类任务”，但这类说法很难被第三方核实——不同实验室用不同机器人、不同布置，评测标准也各不相同。现有排行榜要么不公开细节，要么跑在仿真里，要么规则存在被人钻空子的空间。因此，该领域缺少一个既开放、又可物理复现、还难以作弊的评测标准。

方法：作者设计了一个“机器人密室逃脱”式基准 HATCH。任务分为五个技能类别、三个难度等级，且被串成链：只有传感器确认前一任务完成，下一任务才会被解锁，于是整个房间构成一次长程评测，而非一堆互不相关的单项任务。成功与否由仪器读数判定，不靠人看视频打分；评分规则与机器人具体形态无关，更换硬件也能比较；物体摆放位置由运行当天的随机种子生成，参赛者无法提前排练。

结果与机制：参赛方需提交“自证式”运行记录，包括未剪辑视频、传感器日志和所用随机种子，任何人可据此复核；同时组织不定期线下活动做校准，防止规则被逐渐钻空。所有任务规范、搭建指南、物料清单和评分细则以开放许可发布，其他实验室可以照单复现同一套房间。

意义：这篇论文的核心贡献是一个评测基础设施，而非某个算法。它把“可信、可复现、防作弊”作为设计目标，有望让机器人操作的能力宣称从“作者自述”变成“可被第三方验证的事实”，对推动该领域形成公认排行榜具有基础性价值。
items.comment: 2 pages, 1 table. Accepted at the 5th Workshop on Open Robotics Software, IROS 2026, Pittsburgh, PA, USA. Benchmark repository: https://github.com/shizacharania/hatch-benchmark

rm.usage: 其“传感器判定成功、随机种子摆放、提交未剪辑运行记录”的开放可复现评测范式，可用来设计工程机器人视觉装配任务或哨兵全自主运行的赛前自测与能力认证流程，属评测体系参考而非算法。

items.title_en: MatchCityLoc: Aerial Localization in LoD City Models via Surface Normal Matching
items.title_zh: MatchCityLoc：基于表面法线匹配的LoD城市模型空中定位
items.abstract_en: Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) navigation in urban environments requires precise pose estimation. Because Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals are often unreliable in cities, visual localization serves as a crucial complement. Within this domain, textureless Level-of-Detail (LoD) city models provide a lightweight and privacy-preserving substitute for heavy 3D textured meshes. However, localizing against abstract geometry is challenging. Existing pipelines typically score 2D silhouette overlaps, which can suffer from severe geometric ambiguities. We present MatchCityLoc, a framework that shifts this paradigm to direct feature matching from a noisy 6-DoF pose prior. By extracting surface normals from the query image using a zero-shot foundation model and matching them against rendered LoD normals, we establish explicit 3D-to-2D correspondences. This enables a Perspective-n-Point (PnP) pose solve, which we iteratively refine through a render-and-match loop. Experiments demonstrate strong pose recall and accurate translation and rotation among the evaluated off-the-shelf LoD-based methods with very few renderings. By bridging the modality gap between aerial imagery and texture-free geometry, MatchCityLoc enables accurate localization using lightweight, privacy-preserving city models.

items.title_en: Bio-inspired Thrust-Assisted Trotting on a legged-Aerial Robot via Real-Time QP-MPC
items.title_zh: 受生物启发的推力辅助小跑运动：基于实时QP-MPC的腿足-空中机器人
items.abstract_en: This paper presents the hardware implementation of a quadratic program-based controller on Harpy: thruster-assisted bipedal robot to perform thruster-assisted trotting. This is inspired by wing-assisted locomotion observed in birds such as the chukar partridge, which employ thrust vectoring to manipulate the ground reaction force. The proposed controller formulates the thruster-assisted spring-loaded inverted pendulum dynamics as a condensed QP-based model predictive control problem, enabling simultaneous regulation of ground contact force and active thrust vectoring at 500 Hz. A decoupled control architecture is used, where the robot's sagittal dynamics are controlled using QP-MPC while the frontal dynamics is regulated using a cascade orientation stabilization controller. Two experiments were conducted with different forward reference velocities of 0 m/s and 0.1 m/s. While the instantaneous velocity oscillates, the mean velocities can track their respective reference. Additionally, joint tracking error remains within 1 deg while tracking the desired leg length given by the leg trajectory controller and desired swing trajectory given by Raibert's heuristic. The QP-MPC problem is consistently solved with 0.18ms, which is well within the 2ms computation budget while satisfying the GRF friction cone constraint.
items.comment: To be published in IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026)

items.title_en: Auditing Semantic and Relational Reliability in Open-Vocabulary Human-Object Interaction Evaluation
items.title_zh: 审视开放词汇人-物交互评估中的语义与关系可靠性
items.abstract_en: Open-vocabulary human-object interaction detectors describe interactions in free text, and this creates a problem for evaluation. Category scoring rejects valid paraphrases, while semantic similarity scoring can reward predictions that name the wrong action or reverse the roles of the participants. We present a diagnostic protocol that holds every prediction fixed and scores it under five views, namely official category evaluation, an identity control, lexical normalization, graded semantic credit, and strict propositional equivalence. Comparing these views separates the effect of the matching engine from the effect of semantic credit. The protocol pairs controlled transformations that preserve or break meaning with a blinded audit of natural predictions, and we derive consistency checks that link mean credit, invalid acceptance, and transformation counts. Applied to six systems on HICO-DET, the views disagree on which system leads. GEN-VLKT leads under official evaluation, SL-HOI leads under SHOE, and GEN-VLKT leads again under strict equivalence. Semantic gains range from 1.6 to 20.3 mAP, and AgentHOI keeps less than half of its gain once equivalence is enforced. We recommend that semantic scores be reported together with relational validity and paired uncertainty, so that recovered credit is not read as better interaction understanding.

items.title_en: Validation of Human Motor Development Scales with Humanoid Robots
items.title_zh: 用人形机器人验证人类运动发育量表
items.abstract_en: We investigate how humanoid robots can learn a series of motor skills defined by human infant motor development scales, and we evaluate which scales are comprehensive enough to serve as self-contained guides for developing gross motor skills up to standing and walking. We represent each motor development scale as a developmental graph that guides the training of a humanoid robot. We then apply this graph within a reinforcement learning framework so that the robot learns skills following the natural phases of human motor development described by the scale. Our work demonstrates that graphs derived from three out of four popular pediatric motor scales can successfully guide humanoid robots to develop these skills. The fourth scale misses some intermediate milestones that the other scales have, which causes some failures. After adding a missing milestone in its graph, it also enables the robot to develop those skills successfully.
items.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to ICRA 2027. Video available at https://youtu.be/SR3LUVhohV4

items.title_en: Efficient SAM3 Adaptation for Multi-Class Semantic Segmentation via Dense Competitive Representations
items.title_zh: 通过密集竞争表征实现高效SAM3多类语义分割适配
items.abstract_en: The Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) has achieved significant progress in Promptable Concept Segmentation (PCS) by processing short noun phrases to generate segmentation masks with unique instance identifiers. While SAM3 excels at single-concept segmentation, it falls short in complex, real-world environments where multiple concepts must be segmented simultaneously. In particular, SAM3 typically fails to simultaneously process concepts with semantic overlap, leading to semantic misclassifications and redundant mask predictions. Moreover, as the number of concepts increases, the independent inference paradigm introduces prohibitive inference latency. To address these limitations, we propose the Dense Competitive Representations SAM (DCR-SAM) framework. By decoupling cross-modal interactions, the proposed method alleviates the inference latency. To resolve semantic misclassifications, DCR-SAM dynamically aligns textual concepts with visual representations and incorporates a dense competition head to enforce explicit inter-class competition. Furthermore, a learnable background token is applied to absorb non-target objects dynamically. These mechanisms effectively suppress overlapping predictions and generate high-fidelity masks. Extensive experimental evaluations across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework: (1) achieves a 2.3% $\sim$ 10.7% performance improvement over state-of-the-art methods, (2) delivers a 33$\times$ inference speedup compared to the native SAM3, and (3) exhibits strong robustness across diverse scenarios.
items.comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026. Code is available at https://github.com/set-path/DCR-SAM/tree/main

items.title_en: Decoupling Action from Egocentric Observation for World Simulation
items.title_zh: 将动作与自我中心观测解耦以用于世界仿真
items.abstract_en: Egocentric action transfer aims to decouple the semantic action from egocentric observations and reproduce them in new visual contexts, enabling scalable world simulation, embodied policy learning, and robotic data generation. Existing approaches to transferring actions rely on condition-guided video generation, which converts the observation video into explicit geometric controls (e.g., hand poses or meshes) to drive synthesis. However, these methods introduce geometric estimation errors, making it difficult to preserve physically plausible interactions when transferred to new scenes. Alternatively, motion transfer methods directly extract motion patterns from the observation video, yet motion-level features alone cannot encode rich contact dynamics, frequently leading to severe hand structural collapse and implausible contact layout. To address both limitations, we present EgoACT, a test-time framework for egocentric action transfer that operates directly on the denoising process of video diffusion models without requiring additional geometric estimators. EgoACT uses Velocity-guided Structure Anchoring to stabilize reference-consistent hand-object structure in the early denoising stage, and Sparse Correspondence Calibration to refine reliable local correspondences in the mid-to-late denoising stages. Together, these two components preserve transferable action semantics while improving temporal coherence and interaction realism. We further establish EgoActionBench, a benchmark for evaluating action preservation, visual quality, and hand-object plausibility across diverse egocentric manipulation scenarios. Experiments show that EgoACT generates more coherent and physically plausible interaction videos than strong baselines.
items.comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026, Project page: https://ego-act.github.io/, Code: https://github.com/mayuelala/EgoACT

items.title_en: Energy-Score Stabilized Attentive Mixture-Density Policy: A Lightweight Approach to Multimodal Robot Motion
items.title_zh: 能量分数稳定化的注意力混合密度策略：一种轻量级多模态机器人运动方法
items.abstract_en: For practical motion generation, it is essential to handle multimodality (multiple actions can be correct for the same observation) while maintaining low inference cost and strong generalization from limited demonstrations. We introduce an attentive mixture-density policy trained with the Energy Score that represents future visuomotor trajectories as explicit probability distributions with a single forward pass. Concretely, we output Gaussian mixture parameters for joint commands (and optionally attention points) and optimize them with the Energy Score (computed as a sum of 1D CRPS under a diagonal covariance assumption) instead of the negative log-likelihood (NLL) to avoid MDN singularities and gradient-scale instabilities. Our architecture couples explicit spatial attention with mixture-density outputs, enabling robust multimodal behavior selection under visual noise and small-data regimes. On an 8-DOF manipulator, the method generates distinct avoidance trajectories and stabilizes learning in obstacle avoidance. Moreover, in a randomized moving-object grasping task, where spatiotemporal multimodality and fast timing decisions are required, the proposed model outperforms Diffusion Policy by 15-25% under several unseen conditions, demonstrating superior generalization and real-time feasibility.
items.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Accepted to IROS 2026

items.title_en: From POMDP Theory to Deep RL with Particle Filters
items.title_zh: 从POMDP理论到结合粒子滤波器的深度强化学习
items.abstract_en: Model-based reinforcement learning in partially observable environments requires inferring hidden states, learning latent dynamics, and planning under the resulting belief. Practical algorithms often solve one aspect of the above pipeline while relying on approximations for the others that are often poorly understood, while existing POMDP theory typically analyzes computationally inefficient theoretical algorithms far from modern deep RL practice. To fill this gap, we propose a practical end-to-end algorithm that approximately solves the hidden state filtering problem via sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), updates a latent dynamics model online, and performs approximate online planning for $d$ steps before bootstrapping leaves with a state-value critic (a QMDP approximation). We analyze each approximation and prove an end-to-end regret bound decomposing the error into model estimation error, particle filter error, Monte Carlo rollout error, and a structural bias term induced by the QMDP approximation controllable by the planning depth that we further analyze in various special cases. The resulting guarantee makes explicit how statistical sample size, particle budget, rollout budget, and planning depth affect performance. We instantiate our algorithm in an MPC-based deep RL framework, demonstrating its practicality on a variety of environments. On a POMDP that satisfies our assumptions, each term of the bound decays at its predicted rate. Our results provide a practical and theoretically grounded route for bridging theory and practice within online decision-making in POMDPs.

items.title_en: A latent control model for realistic rodent motion
items.title_zh: 一种用于逼真啮齿动物运动的潜在控制模型
items.abstract_en: The development of embodied models of animal behavior is a major goal of the neuro-AI community. Embodied models will enhance our ability to make direct comparisons between biological and artificial agents. To make such comparisons effective, though, we need embodied models that actually move like animals. Previous work has developed virtual animal bodies and techniques for training realistic motion through imitation. However, to date, there is no system for embodied animal modeling that produces natural movements both during trained goal-directed behavior, and during exploration driven by random generation. Here, we introduce Simulated Control via Augmented Motor Priors for Embodied Reinforcement learning (SCAMPER), a system for training an embodied virtual rat model, enabling natural movements during both goal-directed behavior and random exploration. SCAMPER uses a variational architecture with two distinct priors, a motion prior for control and a behavior prior for exploration. We show that combining both of these priors allows SCAMPER to generate realistic behavior during exploration and exploit the task structure effectively. SCAMPER can also learn from sparse rewards as a result of the diverse movements induced by the behavior prior, allowing the system to model realistic sparse-reward tasks from experimental neuroscience. Altogether, SCAMPER provides the neuro-AI community with an effective new system for training embodied models of rodents on realistic tasks.
items.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 10 pages, 13 figures. Project page with supplementary videos: https://aidansirbu.com/SCAMPER-site/

items.title_en: Scalable, Intuitive, Mixed Reality-Based Semi-Autonomous Robotic Telemanipulation for the Execution of a Fine-Grained Bimanual Task
items.title_zh: 可扩展、直观的混合现实半自主机器人遥操作以执行细粒度双手任务
items.abstract_en: Nowadays, robotic telemanipulation enables humans to control robots so as to execute tasks in a manner similar to how they perform them, and serves as an essential approach for collecting on-robot data for robot learning by human demonstrations. The quality of collected demonstrations directly impacts the performance of the learned policy. However, existing telemanipulation systems rely heavily on human operation, particularly for large-scale data collection. Collecting dozens or hundreds of demonstrations is a demanding process, as operators tend to fatigue quickly, especially during the execution of dexterous tasks that require sustained concentration. Recently, semi-autonomous robotic telemanipulation has emerged as a promising direction that reduces operator workload while preserving human-in-the-loop control for task execution. We therefore introduce a scalable, intuitive, semi-autonomous robotic telemanipulation system that leverages a mixed reality (MR) headset for on-robot data collection. The system autonomously executes the majority of the task trajectories and only requires the operator to make fine adjustments at key stages. We validate the effectiveness of our system by collecting data and training imitation learning policies on the execution of a high-precision, fine-grained bimanual peg-in-hole task. With lower data collection effort, our system obtains high-quality demonstrations that can be used to train fully autonomous task execution policies.
items.comment: 8 pages, 9 figures. Accepted to IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) 2026

items.title_en: Goal Images Are Control Targets: Spatially-Grounded Goal-Image Synthesis for Robotic Manipulation
items.title_zh: 目标图像即控制目标：面向机器人操作的空间接地目标图像合成
items.abstract_en: Goal-conditioned manipulation policies are steered by a goal image, a picture of the desired post-manipulation scene synthesized from the current observation and a language instruction. The prevailing assumption is that better image-editing quality yields better goals, so goal generators are built and compared using general image-editing metrics. We show this assumption is false. Across two independent goal-conditioned policies on CALVIN, the image editors that top aggregate editing-quality leaderboards (Gemini 3 Pro Image and GPT Image 1.5) produce worse control targets than our proposed far smaller finetuned open models, and the gap widens sharply for the multi-step (long-horizon) tasks robots actually face. A per-dimension analysis explains why. Downstream policy success is governed almost entirely by manipulation adherence (selecting the right object and the right final state; Spearman $ρ\approx 0.9$ with success), while photorealism and aesthetic fidelity, precisely where large proprietary editors excel, are uncorrelated with success ($ρ\approx 0$). This dissociation holds on both CALVIN and the real-world-aligned SIMPLER-Bridge benchmark. We then present SGE-Goal, a spatially-grounded decomposed editing framework that predicts initial and final 2D edit-region masks before goal-image synthesis. SGE-Goal turns open base models (FLUX.1 Kontext, FLUX.2 klein) into the strongest goal generators we evaluate on CALVIN, and second only to Gemini 3 Pro Image on SIMPLER-Bridge. Base models fine-tuned with SGE-Goal also hold up under chaining far better than the best proprietary editor, sustaining roughly seven times the success rate at the longest (five-step) chains. We release code, datasets, checkpoints, and a human-aligned diagnostic evaluator. Our results argue that goal generators must be selected by downstream utility, not by editing-quality leaderboards.

items.title_en: CondenseVLA: Learnable History Condensation for Efficient Multi-Frame VLA
items.title_zh: CondenseVLA：面向高效多帧VLA的可学习历史压缩
items.abstract_en: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. However, injecting historical information solely by enlarging the history window is computationally costly and frequently yields limited gains due to substantial redundancy and task-agnostic, inflexible sampling of observations. We propose CondenseVLA, a multi-frame VLA policy with a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for using short-term visual context in action decoding. Given a sequence of cached per-frame features from the VLM backbone, CondenseVLA distills observation history into a fixed set of slot tokens using learnable queries and multi-head cross-attention. Simple auxiliary regularization penalizes overlap among slot attention maps and decorrelates slot embeddings, encouraging complementary attention and reducing slot redundancy. Across the evaluated tasks, CondenseVLA improves Simpler-WidowX success from 58.7% to 69.8% (+11.1 percentage points), achieves 97.2% on LIBERO, and reaches 52.8% on real-world tasks. It achieves 21.6% success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks. These results support selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA
items.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 39 pages, including supplementary material and the NeurIPS paper checklist. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA

items.title_en: CODA: Cohort- and Drift-aware Foundation Model for Multimodal Clinical Reasoning
items.title_zh: CODA：面向多模态临床推理的队列与漂移感知基础模型
items.abstract_en: Recent advances in multimodal foundation models have demonstrated strong performance across diverse clinical tasks. However, existing approaches predominantly operate at the individual sample level and fail to model the interplay between population-level cohort patterns and patient-specific variation that underlie real-world clinical reasoning. In practice, clinicians routinely reason through patient cohorts sharing similar demographic, physiological, or pathological characteristics, while accounting for patient-specific deviations from the group prototype. Motivated by this gap, we propose CODA, a cohort- and drift-aware foundation model for multimodal clinical reasoning. CODA explicitly integrates cohort structure into the modeling pipeline through two complementary mechanisms: cohort-aware population stratification and drift-aware individual adaptation. In particular, we leverage reinforcement learning to discover clinically meaningful patient cohorts, and further model each patient's deviation from cohort prototypes as a structured drift signal encoding fine-grained individual heterogeneity. These cohort- and drift-aware representations are incorporated into the foundation model to enable reasoning that is simultaneously informed by population-level patterns and sensitive to individual-level variation. Extensive experiments on real-world electronic health record (EHR) benchmarks demonstrate that CODA achieves consistent effectiveness and strong generalizability across diverse clinical tasks, including closed-QA, open-QA, and report generation.

items.title_en: BodyBridge: Grounded Body Layers for Sim-to-Real Translation of Vulnerable Road Users
items.title_zh: BodyBridge：用于弱势道路使用者仿真到现实迁移的具身身体层
items.abstract_en: Simulation-to-real driving video diffusion models can translate photorealistic scenes, but they typically represent pedestrians and cyclists, vulnerable road users (VRUs), as generic object classes. This is insufficient for vulnerable road users whose safety-relevant appearance depends on articulated pose and identity. We present BodyBridge and Grounded Body Layers (GBL), a simulator-derived, pixel-aligned representation that combines scene geometry, canonical per-pixel body correspondence, and exact VRU masks. GBL provides explicit articulation to the video diffusion model, emphasizes VRU regions during control-branch post-training, and supports additive composition with scene-geometry control at inference. It also enables per-joint evaluation of generated VRUs and a failure taxonomy for identity errors. On CARLA-to-real translation, BodyBridge improves near-range PCK@0.5 by 22% over the released depth-conditioned baseline. Replacing normal-map body control with canonical correspondence reduces body flips by 18%, while composition reduces near-range facing flips by 27%. These results show that explicit body grounding complements scene-level control and improves pose-faithful VRU generation. All code, data, and model checkpoints will be made publicly available to support reproducible, pedestrian-aware autonomous driving research.

items.title_en: Towards Reinforcement Learning for Space Robotics: Fast Training and Reliable Real-World Transfer
items.title_zh: 面向空间机器人的强化学习：快速训练与可靠的真实世界迁移
items.abstract_en: This work demonstrates the use of a fast simulation-based training framework to learn control policies using reinforcement learning. The hardware requirements are minimal and the simulation-learned policies transfer reliably to the real world. With this setup, we show that a quadruped robot can learn to traverse diverse real-world terrains reliably---including in a lunar-analog facility---after less than 20 minutes of training on a single consumer-grade GPU. These results provide a glimpse of a future where reinforcement learning is a crucial tool in developing more capable and robust space robotic systems. Video demonstrations are available at https://youtu.be/vUFJiZdJaQ0.
items.comment: Presented at the Space Robotics Workshop at IROS 2026

items.title_en: BiDex-100: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across 100+ Simulation Tasks
items.title_zh: BiDex-100：面向100+仿真任务的双手灵巧操作综合基准
items.abstract_en: Bimanual manipulation with dexterous hands has attracted growing attention in research on robotic action models. However, few studies have developed benchmarks specifically tailored for dexterous manipulation, leaving the dexterous manipulation capabilities of existing models insufficiently characterized. In this paper, we present BiDex-100, a simulation benchmark for bimanual dexterous manipulation that combines broad task coverage, multi-dimensional evaluation, and high-DoF hand embodiments. Concretely, the benchmark comprises 106 tasks organized along five capability axes: generalization, instruction following, limited demonstrations, long horizon, and memory. Each task is paired with an out-of-domain variant featuring controlled visual and spatial changes, allowing systematic assessment of robustness. In addition, the benchmark supports two embodiments and provides 8,080 success-validated teleoperated demonstrations, totaling 6.25 million frames. We evaluate seven recent Vision-Language-Action models under a unified protocol, establishing baselines for capability-specific performance, robustness, and data efficiency. The website is available at https://BiDex-100.github.io/BiDex-100/.

rm.usage: 双手灵巧操作仿真基准，其任务与评测维度可参考用于工程机器人机械臂装配任务的仿真设计与评估，但任务本体（桌面灵巧操作）与装配 42mm 发射机构差异较大。

items.title_en: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
items.title_zh: UniWALM：面向具身机器人控制的统一世界动作语言模型
items.abstract_en: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).

rm.usage: 统一世界-动作-语言模型偏具身操作与记忆型任务，与本赛自瞄、雷达、决策核心链路关联弱，最多作为多模态决策研究的远期参考。

items.title_en: Physical Canvas: A Vision Tactile World Model For Robot Policy Evaluation And Learning
items.title_zh: Physical Canvas：用于机器人策略评估与学习的视觉触觉世界模型
items.abstract_en: Evaluating and post-training robot policies through physical interaction is costly and difficult to scale, motivating action-conditioned world models as interactive simulators. However, visually plausible predictions can misrepresent contact dynamics, providing unreliable feedback for policy evaluation and learning. We introduce PhysCanvas, a state-consistent visuo-tactile world model for contact-rich robot manipulation. PhysCanvas unifies multi-view RGB, tactile images, marker displacement, task state, and actions within a unified vision space. All modalities share a video VAE and pretrained generative backbone, allowing optical touch to reuse visual and temporal priors. Motion images derived through forward kinematics and camera projection provide spatially aligned action conditioning, while an initial RGB anchor and updated reference observations guide sequential generation. Our consistency-aware post-training uses the frozen Scene Reward Model, Modality Reward Model, and State Reward Model to supervise scene preservation, visual-tactile compatibility, and agreement with real task outcomes. The resulting world model supports closed-loop policy rollouts for evaluation and provides imagined interactions and rewards for GRPO policy updates. Across four real-world manipulation tasks, when policies are rolled out in the world model, State Reward Model supervision increases the arithmetic mean of task-wise Pearson correlations between world-model and real-world success rates from 0.602 to 0.885. Policy post-training in the reward-guided world model further increases $π_{0.5}$'s mean real-world success rate from a 59.1% SFT baseline to 70.8%. These results demonstrate the value of unified multimodal modeling and consistency-aware post-training for robot policy evaluation and learning. Project page: https://zebinx.github.io/PhysCanvas_HomePage/.

rm.usage: 视觉-触觉世界模型用于接触丰富操作策略的评估，可设想用于工程机器人装配过程的策略评估，但本赛工程装配以视觉位姿为主、缺少触觉，实用性低。

items.title_en: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
items.title_zh: AgenticRoboRL：将编码智能体后训练引入智能体机器人
items.abstract_en: Agentic robotics systems combine planners with robot harnesses to perform complex manipulation tasks. Recent work improves these systems through better harnesses and external memory, but relies on powerful closed-source models as planners and does not improve the planners' own capabilities. In contrast, coding agents have improved substantially by post-training the model itself. We therefore investigate whether post-training can also improve robot planners. However, applying it across robot harnesses requires accommodating different execution mechanisms, including VLA skill invocation and control-code generation. To this end, we introduce AgenticRoboRL, a framework for post-training robot planners across different harnesses. The training recipe combines supervised fine-tuning with multi-turn reinforcement learning. To accommodate different execution mechanisms, harness-specific adapters connect recorded planner interactions with task outcomes, enabling a common RL training pipeline while keeping execution components fixed. On LIBERO-PRO, AgenticRoboRL raises the success rate of a 9B-parameter planner from 18.1% to 71.0% without external memory, approaching the 72.1% achieved by Codex (GPT-5.5) with external memory. These results demonstrate post-training as an effective approach for improving robot planners. We will release the framework and trained planner checkpoints.

items.title_en: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images
items.title_zh: SceneRig：用于从单张图像重建仿真就绪3D场景的智能体系统
items.abstract_en: Simulation is a powerful tool for robotics, but building diverse, simulation-ready scenes at scale remains difficult. Reconstructing scenes from single images is a promising alternative, but visual similarity alone is insufficient: objects must also be recovered, accurately placed, and physically grounded. Existing methods that rely on post-hoc physics settling often misplace objects, producing scenes that look correct but behave poorly under manipulation. We present SceneRig, an agentic system that turns a single image into an editable, simulation-ready scene. SceneRig combines geometric, visual, and physical tools to reconstruct a faithful 3D scene. An agent then performs edit-and-validate loops inside a physics simulator to achieve physical stability. Across diverse inputs, SceneRig improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement while keeping the reconstructed scenes physically stable. Furthermore, SceneRig is effective for downstream robotics: its scenes predict real-robot policy outcomes more accurately than the baseline method and more reliably support replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.
items.comment: Accepted at CoRL 2026 Agentic Robotics Workshop. Project page: https://red-fairy.github.io/SceneRig/

items.title_en: Continuous-Time Policy Gradient from Discrete Data: Convergence Analysis and Model-Free Algorithms
items.title_zh: 基于离散数据的连续时间策略梯度：收敛性分析与无模型算法
items.abstract_en: Continuous-time reinforcement learning seeks an optimal policy under unknown dynamics driven by stochastic differential equations using observations collected at discrete times. We develop a policy gradient framework that combines rigorous convergence analysis with learning from discrete data. We first establish a performance difference lemma and derive policy gradient formulas for randomized and parametrized policies. We then prove exponential convergence of an entropy-regularized policy flow to the regularized optimum. For discrete parametrized updates, we derive a convergence bound that explicitly separates the contributions of critic error, policy-regression error, and the learning step size. To enable learning under unknown dynamics, we integrate this framework with PhiBE, which constructs a continuous-time surrogate generator from discrete transition data. The resulting on-policy and off-policy model-free actor-critic algorithms preserve the continuous-time structure of the control problem. Numerical experiments on an entropy-regularized linear-quadratic regulator and a nonlinear wheeled robot demonstrate the performance and stability of the proposed methods with both known and data-driven dynamics.

rm.usage: 连续时间策略梯度理论，与RM常用的离散仿真RL训练不直接匹配，仅对sim中高保真连续动力学训练有理论参考。

items.title_en: MAPLE: Mondrian-Anchored Prior for Learning-free Indoor Exploration
items.title_zh: MAPLE：用于免学习室内探索的蒙德里安锚定先验
items.abstract_en: Robots exploring unknown indoor environments must decide where to move while much of the environment remains unseen. Predicting the occupancy of unseen space beyond the current sensor range can improve these decisions, but recent approaches commonly rely on learned models that require offline training and repeated inference during exploration. We introduce the Mondrian-Anchored Prior for Learning-free Indoor Exploration (MAPLE), a training-free predictive approach that adapts the Mondrian process into an online generative prior conditioned on observed geometric cues in the current partial map. MAPLE generates multiple plausible map hypotheses and evaluates visibility separately within each to estimate frontier gain, preserving differences in predicted visibility across hypotheses. Across KTH floor-plans and real-SLAM environments at multiple sensor ranges, MAPLE consistently improves over non-predictive exploration and remains competitive with learned predictive approaches. Its lightweight procedural construction enables predictive exploration with limited computational resources. Experimental results further show that more accurate map prediction does not necessarily produce better exploration, highlighting the importance of how predictions are represented and used in exploration decisions.

rm.usage: 无学习室内探索先验可用于哨兵在地图缺失或未知区域的探索决策，但RM哨兵通常在已知赛场运行，需改造成已知地图下的路径规划辅助。

items.title_en: Learning Computational Structure for Sample-Efficient Prediction
items.title_zh: 面向样本高效预测的计算结构学习
items.abstract_en: Statistical learning in high dimensions suffers from the curse of dimensionality. Fortunately, many functions of practical interest are compositionally sparse, meaning they admit a composition of local functions, each depending on only a few variables, allowing sample complexity to depend on local arity rather than ambient dimension. Yet realizing this benefit requires exploiting hidden compositional structure, which theory does not establish for practical gradient-based training. We study this gap with CSFRBench, a controlled benchmark that hides the target's compositional computation during training but retains it for diagnosis, and find that dense networks and sparsity-based baselines leave much of that benefit unrealized. Inspired by the spatial organization of biological neural circuits, we introduce Learned Wiring (LeWi): each neuron has a learned low-dimensional embedding, only nearby neurons connect, and embeddings and weights are trained jointly. LeWi improves sample efficiency on targets with hierarchical structure, intermediate reuse, or independent modules. Across 32 additional targets generated by independently sampled computation graphs, LeWi is the most sample-efficient method not given the target graph, with 27% lower mean learning-curve area than dense networks. Dense networks perform better on targets with a single high-arity function. LeWi's representations and connectivity align with the target computation. On 17 world-model prediction tasks spanning control, navigation, and manipulation, LeWi beats the dense baseline on 16 and wins 99/119 baseline comparisons. These results show that jointly learning connectivity and weights can exploit computational structure to improve sample efficiency.

rm.usage: 样本高效学习理论，对sim中强化学习训练样本效率有间接启发，但离自瞄、导航、决策等RM具体任务落地很远。

items.title_en: CoGaussian: Open-Vocabulary Gaussian-based Collaborative 3D Scene Understanding
items.title_zh: CoGaussian：开放词汇的基于高斯的协同3D场景理解
items.abstract_en: Collaborative perception enables agents to retrieve the scene semantics and geometry beyond the field of view of any individual agent. This broader scene understanding enhances transportation safety and improves efficiency in multi-robot systems. However, existing collaborative semantic occupancy methods rely on dense 3D voxel annotations and are limited to recognizing objects within a predefined set of semantic classes. To overcome these limitations, we present CoGaussian, an open-vocabulary Gaussian-based collaborative semantic occupancy prediction framework. CoGaussian represents a scene as a set of foundation model-aligned sparse 3D Gaussians, which serve as a compact representation for communicating and fusing geometric and semantic information across multiple agents. On the Semantic-OPV2V benchmark, our method outperforms existing open-vocabulary single-agent approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of open-vocabulary collaborative scene understanding.

rm.usage: 开放词汇协同3D语义占据可借鉴到雷达与多机协同感知，用于融合多视角信息生成敌方位置与语义地图；但需适配RM传感器与实时性要求。

items.title_en: VLM-Guided Contact Retargeting and Generative Partner Modeling for Humanoid-Human Interaction
items.title_zh: VLM引导的接触重定向与生成式伙伴建模，用于人形机器人-人类交互
items.abstract_en: Humanoid-human interaction requires robots to operate under severe partial observability: during close physical contact, the human partner is occluded, truncated, or outside the robot's field of view, causing pose estimation to fail and often necessitating external tracking or privileged human state. At the same time, heavy mutual occlusions introduce errors into the human-human motion-capture data used for learning. We present REACT, a framework for learning deployable humanoid-human interaction policies from human-human demonstrations. REACT treats semantic contact structure as the key supervisory signal connecting demonstration processing, interaction learning, and onboard control. First, a VLM-guided contact modeling and retargeting pipeline identifies semantically meaningful contacts and transfers them onto humanoid-human geometry while preserving interaction structure. Using these annotations, privileged interaction policies learn physically grounded behaviors through interaction-aware contact rewards and are then distilled into deployable egocentric depth policies trained entirely from onboard sensing using photorealistic human depth rendering. To address severe partial observability, we introduce generative partner-state modeling objectives that predict partner motion from occluded egocentric views. We evaluate REACT in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid across five contact-rich interactions. Semantic contact modeling substantially improves preservation of demonstrated interactions, while generative partner-state modeling improves contact recall on four of five interactions, most under heavy occlusion. On real hardware, REACT performs all five interactions using onboard sensing alone.

items.title_en: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
items.title_zh: SuperMimic：利用单一可微世界模型扩展人形机器人全身控制
items.abstract_en: Tracking large human-motion datasets has become the dominant route to general, expressive humanoid whole-body control, but scaling across many motions is expensive. Current pipelines use model-free reinforcement learning, either merging per-motion specialists through lossy distillation, or brute-forcing a single policy with cluster-scale compute. SuperMimic amortizes learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of their shared dynamics, fit from logged transitions of a standard rigid-body simulator. The world model and the tracking policy train together in one loop, and backpropagation-through-time over short imagined rollouts gives the policy analytic gradients. Fast imagined rollouts and analytic gradients make policy learning efficient. In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than $1000\times$ and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. From 1 to 264 hours of motion, the world model's prediction error stays stable, and GPU-hours to a target return grow slowly. Our policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions. SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws.
items.comment: Accepted at CoRL 2026 (Oral). Project website: https://supermimic.github.io

rm.usage: 人形全身控制的世界模型训练，与RM机器人形态和控制任务不符；仅世界模型思路对sim/RL训练有很弱的参考。

items.title_en: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training
items.title_zh: 以用户的语言变体作答：面向后训练的校准适应配对
items.abstract_en: People adapt how they talk to the person in front of them. However, chat models tend to respond in Standard English regardless of the dialect used by the user. A uniform answer can hide whether training treats these users alike, and output audits cannot tell as well. We trace how each post-training stage, from supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning, changes a model's tendency to match the user, and read what each update prefers from two content-matched replies, one matching the user and one not. Across 10 open model lineages, post-training standardizes replies to every informal cue, yet after adjusting for how likely each reply already was, the DPO update still favours matching British and Australian spelling over AAE and Singlish on 10 lineages, and models still produce AAE features when asked. We then introduce calibrated accommodation pairs (CAP), preference data that reward matching users' dialect density while preserving Standard English for Standard-English users. On a fully open model, CAP raises convergence on features it was not trained on without a detectable increase in dialect for Standard-English users or a cost in instruction following. In contrast, one-sided pairs reach a similar gain only by overshooting the user and imposing dialect. Our findings show that uniform replies can hide selective updates and audits should read the update as well as the output. Code: https://github.com/kouzhizhuo/cap-accommodation.

items.title_en: Fast Motion Retargeting Pipeline for Scalable Humanoid Robot Learning
items.title_zh: 面向可扩展人形机器人学习的快速运动重定向流水线
items.abstract_en: While large-scale human motion capture datasets provide a rich source of demonstrations for humanoid robot learning, retargeting the diverse motions to different humanoid robots remains a nontrivial challenge. Existing kinodynamic trajectory optimization pipelines are computationally expensive and often require manual adjustments per motion. We present FRDV (Fast Retargeting with Dynamics Validation), a scalable framework consisting of rapid constrained kinematic retargeting and an additional dynamics validation pipeline. Its kinematic stage integrates a custom Sequential Quadratic Programming solver, Real-Time Iteration, and parallel chunk-based processing, achieving up to 9,156 frames per second, approximately up to 136 times faster than GMR and ProtoMotions, while robot-specific constraints are incorporated into the optimization to reduce common retargeting artifacts, such as ground penetration and self-collision. For motions requiring additional verification, a contact implicit iLQR controller is utilized to test the retargeted reference under full rigid body dynamics. This dynamics-based validation identifies dynamically infeasible motions and refines contact-related artifacts such as foot floating and foot skating. We evaluate retargeting quality by training motion tracking reinforcement learning policies using several state-of-the-art pipelines and comparing their tracking fidelity and success rates. Furthermore, sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated on a Unitree G1 humanoid. Videos and code are available at: https://daroslab.github.io/frdv/.

items.title_en: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
items.title_zh: GPT-6-Astra理解触觉并超越视觉—触觉—语言—动作模型
items.abstract_en: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action. GPT-6-Astra combines this context with multimodal observations and interaction history to generate control commands and adjust actions through contact feedback. Without additional robotics-specific pretraining or per-task policy fine-tuning, our method achieves 93.8\% mean success across five UniVTAC tasks. Overall performance is comparable to state-of-the-art policies, with higher success on selected tasks. On Insert Hole, tactile feedback improves success from 31\% to 99\%. Execution analysis further demonstrates contact-guided probing and correction, supporting manipulation progress through explicit expert experience and online feedback.

items.title_en: Physical AI for Intralogistics: Benchmarking the NVIDIA Sim-to-Real Ecosystem for Cosmos-Enhanced COMPASS Navigation on Industrial Mobile Robots
items.title_zh: 面向内部物流的物理AI：在工业移动机器人上对用于Cosmos增强COMPASS导航的NVIDIA Sim-to-Real生态系统进行基准测试
items.abstract_en: Classical robot navigation stacks are reliable but often require re-engineering for each new robot type and site. Learning-based navigation shifts this effort from hand-tuned parameters to data generation and training, where a policy adapts to each new embodiment or facility by fine-tuning in simulation. Whether policies adapted this way stay reliable on real industrial robots has seen little systematic testing. We study this for NVIDIA's X-Mobility and COMPASS workflow for training learned navigation policies on Idealworks robots. In simulation, we extend the COMPASS benchmark with two embodiments, the differential-drive iw.hub and an omnidirectional Humanoid Mobile Platform (HMP), and with a digital twin of the Idealworks R&D center. For the real world, we fine-tune X-Mobility on data from this digital twin, with and without sim-to-real variants generated by NVIDIA Cosmos, train COMPASS on top of it from scratch in the digital twin, deploy the resulting policies on the iw.hub's onboard Jetson AGX Xavier, and benchmark them in the Idealworks R&D center against COMPASS trained only on NVIDIA's environments and the existing Idealworks navigation stack on task success, efficiency, safety, smoothness and onboard compute. Running every static scenario both in a digital-twin replica and in the real facility measures the sim-to-real gap and how far Cosmos-augmented data closes it. Training in the digital twin with Cosmos sim-to-real augmentation raises the real-world success rate of learned navigation from 65.3% to 91.7% across four scenarios and nearly halves its weighted travel time compared with simulation-only training, bringing it within 8.3 points of the production navigation stack, fully onboard; with an integrated global planner, it also reaches far, occluded goals in every trial.

items.title_en: Plausible Future, Wrong Choice: Steering World-Action Models toward Intended Future
items.title_zh: 看似合理的未来，错误的选择：引导世界-动作模型走向预期未来
items.abstract_en: World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied generalist policies by jointly modeling future world evolution and robot actions across diverse manipulation tasks. However, representing diverse futures is only the first step: a capable WAM must also generate futures that match the requirements of the current task and execution progress. In long-horizon manipulation where similar observation-action segments occur across different tasks and stages, existing approaches may generate locally plausible yet misdirected rollouts to drift toward wrong task stage, i.e., a phenomenon we term Stage Confusion. To address this problem, we propose TaskWAM, a closed-loop, stage-aware framework that represents fine-grained task requirements with Mode Tokens and tracks execution progress with State Tokens, forming a structured task state to steer world--action generation toward intended future. We further introduce StageBench, a controlled multi-stage manipulation benchmark with parameterized stage variations and automated evaluation.Extensive experiments on both simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks demonstrate that TaskWAM effectively reduces confusion and achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, TaskWAM provides strong plug-and-play transfer across heterogeneous WAM architectures and robot embodiments, including single-arm robots, dual-arm grippers, dexterous hands, and humanoid robots.

rm.usage: 世界-动作模型对长时序任务的未来引导思路，可用于工程机器人多阶段装配任务的阶段判别，但与 RM 实时对抗场景差距较大，关联偏弱。

items.title_en: SPAR: Search-trained Push Action Ranker for Efficient Navigation Among Movable Obstacles
items.title_zh: SPAR：搜索训练的推动动作排序器，用于可移动障碍物环境中的高效导航
items.abstract_en: Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) requires a robot to rearrange objects that block access to its goal. For a pushing robot, progress may depend on a setup push that enables a later opening without itself clearing a passage. The number of candidate sequences can grow exponentially with sequence length, making physics-based search costly. We introduce the Search-trained Push Action Ranker (SPAR), which learns to prioritize push primitives from simulated search outcomes. Searches over sequences of up to two pushes per object provide supervision that distinguishes immediate openings from setup pushes. A transformer trained with regression and ranking losses scores primitives using contact tokens conditioned on scene geometry and reachability regions. The same model guides simulator evaluations in SPAR Search and selects actions for direct execution in SPAR Policy. Both modes solve successive keyhole problems that open access to neighboring free-space regions within a NAMO planner. Across successful runs on $300$ simulated two-push keyhole problems, SPAR Search reduces median simulator calls by $7.0\times$, leading to a $3.8\times$ reduction in planning time relative to Random Search. Without retraining, the same ranker guides search on $600$ keyhole problems which have no solution within two pushes. At a depth limit of five pushes, SPAR Search achieves $50.7\%$ success within $100$ simulator calls, compared with $20.2\%$ for Random Search. These gains carry over to NAMO planning: on hard simulated scenes, SPAR Search achieves $47\%$ success within $100$ simulator calls, compared with $21\%$ for Random Search. In real-robot experiments, SPAR Policy succeeds in $37/40$ trials without a physics-based digital twin, compared with $33/40$ for SPAR Search and $27/40$ for Random Search.

items.title_en: Reinforced Iterative Learning Control for elastic joint arms: Guaranteed cross-trajectory generalization under model uncertainties
items.title_zh: 弹性关节臂的强化迭代学习控制：模型不确定性下保证跨轨迹泛化
items.abstract_en: Trajectory tracking for compliant robots is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics and modeling uncertainties, often requiring learning-based methods to avoid explicit parameter identification. Iterative Learning Control (ILC) ensures theoretically high precision and preserves the passive compliance of the robot. However, traditional ILC requires a separate learning phase for each new trajectory. Conversely, Reinforcement Learning (RL) generalizes to new trajectories, but practically suffers from high sample complexity and limited tracking precision. This work proposes Reinforced Iterative Learning Control (RILC) that combines the strengths of both approaches to achieve fast adaptation and guaranteed tracking convergence across diverse trajectories. By establishing a concurrent coupling between the two controllers, RILC overcomes the high initial errors and slow adaptation of traditional ILC, enabling high-performance tracking from the very first trials. In this architecture, ILC provides high-quality samples, while RL contributes as a generalizing best-effort policy across iterations. Additionally, a theoretical proof is presented to show that the RL component preserves ILC stability and, under specific conditions, can also reduce the error bound asymptotically. The efficacy of this framework is demonstrated through simulation and experiments on an underactuated 4-degree-of-freedom serial elastic robot using different trajectories and modeling mismatches.
items.comment: Accepted for publication in Control Engineering Practice, 2026. 16 pages, 10 figures

items.title_en: GALA: Geometry-Aware Language Model for Controllable Object Arrangement
items.title_zh: GALA：用于可控物体布置的几何感知语言模型
items.abstract_en: Reasoning about fine-grained placement constraints, such as support and containment, is essential for realistic 3D scene creation. It remains a significant challenge for existing methods that rely on simplified object representations like oriented bounding box (OBB), which are blind to the detailed geometry. To address this limitation, we introduce GALA, a geometry-aware language model with explicit point cloud perception for controllable object placement. Our model performs autoregressively by predicting the 6D pose of one target object at a time conditioned on the scene context and placement instruction. We utilize a two-stage training strategy: the first stage aligns geometric and textual modalities through pretraining tasks, and the second stage fine-tunes the model for placement. To facilitate this task, we also curate a multi-source scene dataset covering diverse room types and fine-grained furniture arrangements, which will be open-sourced for community benefit. Experiments on our benchmark show our model significantly outperforms baselines without explicit geometric reasoning. We further develop a multi-stage plan-place-verify agent pipeline that uses the model for text-driven scene generation. Project Page: https://xccelephant.github.io/paper/gala/
items.comment: Accepted to SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers. Project Page: https://xccelephant.github.io/paper/gala/

items.title_en: Large Multimodal Models for Direct Robot Control: GPT-6 as a Beginning
items.title_zh: 用于直接机器人控制的大型多模态模型：以GPT-6为开端
items.abstract_en: Recent advances in visuospatial understanding and agentic reasoning enable direct robotic manipulation with general-purpose multimodal models, but their embodied capabilities remain poorly understood. This paper systematically evaluate GPT-6 Astra for closed-loop robotic manipulation using a lightweight agent execution framework. We first probe three fundamental embodied capabilities-depth perception, embodied in-context learning, and tactile understanding-and demonstrate that the model can exploit depth information, acquire simple manipulation strategies from contextual demonstrations, and use tactile feedback to correct its actions. We then evaluate GPT-6 Astra across five established manipulation benchmarks along six capability dimensions. Despite competitive performance on several benchmarks-26.92\% success on RoboDojo and 76.0\% on RoboTwin 2.0-our analysis reveals a pronounced gap between semantic reasoning and physical execution, particularly in consequence-aware action planning, precision, and complex motion coordination. To further examine these limitations, we introduce LIBERO-GeoMotion, a new benchmark of geometry-constrained tasks that require precise pose alignment, coordinated translation and rotation, and anticipation of physical action consequences. GPT-6 Astra achieves only 11.1\% zero-shot success, exposing the difficulty of translating spatial understanding into physically feasible motion. Real-world experiments corroborate these findings: zero-shot execution is feasible for simple tasks, yet persistent deficits remain in motion feasibility, precise control, and physical safety, while substantial inference latency further hinders practical deployment. Overall, our results characterize the emerging embodied capabilities of general-purpose multimodal models and delineate the key challenges toward safe, efficient, and reliable robotic manipulation.

items.title_en: Reframing Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning: From Absolute to Relative Representations
items.title_zh: 重新审视以物体为中心的强化学习：从绝对表示到相对表示
items.abstract_en: Object-centric reinforcement learning agents typically receive each object's position in a fixed global frame, even though their decisions usually depend on where objects are relative to one another. These absolute views often fail to capture the local context that is most relevant to the agent's behavior. As a result, an agent must relearn the same response at every location where a configuration can occur, and its performance collapses when the scene is merely shifted. In this work, we propose a shift toward Object-Relative Coordinates fixed to Anchor (ORCA), where entities are described in a relative frame of reference. To operationalize this idea, we introduce Object-Relative inductive-Bias Transformers (ORBiT), a transformer-based architecture for processing anchor-relative inputs in reinforcement learning. Our results suggest these relative representations improve performance for both MLP and transformer agents. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ORBiT outperforms the pixel-based PPO baseline, achieving an aggregate HNS IQM greater than 1.0 over 13 Atari games. ORBiT learns the game of Foosball from scratch, dominating all baselines. In our controlled Tag environment, we further show that ORCA extends to rotations, that ORBiT generalizes to unseen numbers of distractors, and that these gains require a decision-relevant anchor.

items.title_en: Reasoning as a Distribution: Generative Plan Latents for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.title_zh: 推理即分布：面向视觉-语言-动作模型的生成式规划潜变量
items.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies increasingly reason before acting, but existing reasoning models compress this intermediate decision into a single representation. When several plans are valid, this commitment hides alternatives that could otherwise be selected or revised. We introduce the Generative Plan Latent (GPL), which represents the reasoning state as a low-dimensional conditional distribution over plans, such as which object, grasp, or route to use. This makes the reasoning state addressable: without retraining the VLA, plans can be sampled (coverage), selected on request (steering), and reweighted by deployment outcomes (outcome adaptation). We test all three on SimplerEnv manipulation with $π_0$, and extend the analysis to RoboCasa, LIBERO, and a maze domain. Steering the plan raises the fraction of executions that follow the request from 0.48 to 0.94, while the same guidance on the native action distribution shows no reliable gain. Finally, we show that an explicit plan is most useful when it carries decision information not already determined by the observation.

items.title_en: From Predictive Geometry to Action: Learning Complementary Predictive Representations for Embodied Manipulation
items.title_zh: 从预测几何到动作：为具身操作学习互补预测表征
items.abstract_en: Effective manipulation requires a policy to capture not only about the current scene geometry, but also about how that geometry will evolve under interaction. Existing approaches either augment policies with geometric information from current observations or introduce future prediction as auxiliary supervision, leaving open how predictive geometry should be represented for action generation. Therefore, we propose a two-stage framework, which learns complementary predictive representations from multi-view video clips. During pretraining, a frozen 3D foundation model provides dense geometric features that are compressed into predictive geometric representations and optimized to preserve scene structure and its temporal evolution. Action supervision is then applied to geometric transitions to extract a complementary motor representation that emphasizes action-relevant transitions. During downstream post-training, predictive geometry is transferred through geometry queries, while the motor representation guides intermediate features along the action-generation pathway. Future observations are used only as privileged supervision during training and are not required at inference time. Across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, SimplerEnv, and real-world bimanual and single-arm tasks, our approach consistently improves downstream policies, including an absolute gain of 10.4 percentage points on the WidowX evaluation. We further demonstrate transfer across multiple VLA architectures and WAMs, with improvements in both future-world and action prediction. The code will be available at https://github.com/xuxiaoxxxx/CPR.
